title: People Ops reflection & 1:1 prep — Q1 2026
content:
Quick context:
- Personal scratchpad for my manager 1:1 this week and a working log of wins / signals I care about for my FY26 career thread. Keep informal.
- Role: People Ops (partnering primarily with Eng, Platform & Product). Focus areas: hiring funnel, offer velocity, onboarding quality, and manager enablement.

Wins / highlights (Q1):
- Reduced offer-to-accept median from 6.2 days to 4.0 days for senior IC roles by standardizing compensation bands + templated candidate comms. Small process change but measurable.
- Piloted a 2-week onboarding cohort for infra-eng new hires; first cohort NPS 8/10 (n=9) and ramp check-ins show 20% fewer early-week infra tickets.
- Launched manager office hours with weekly drop-in; first month attendance 28 unique managers, got direct feedback that the template for career ladders clarified expectations.

Concrete examples I will cite in 1:1:
- Offer velocity: offer J-58 (senior infra eng) — moved from verbal to offer in 72 hours using new comp template; candidate accepted and started 2026-02-09.
- Onboarding: cohort notes + feedback summary (see linked PR). Highlight: removing duplicated tooling walkthrough saved ~3 hours from orientation deck.
- Manager enablement: internal survey comment from L4 manager: "The ladder examples made calibration feels doable" — cite exact quote in 1:1.

Metrics I care about (signals, tracked):
- Time-to-offer (median) — current: 4.0 days (down from 6.2)
- Offer accept rate (rolling 90d) — current: 81%
- New-hire ramp to independent shipping (median weeks) — baseline 12w, cohort shows 10w (early)
- Manager confidence score (monthly pulse) — current: 6.9/10

Areas I want to own / stretch into (ask during 1:1):
- Lead a cross-functional effort to define hiring service-levels for product vs infra (we need distinct SLAs).
- Pilot an automated candidate comms workflow (ops + legal) to reduce manual follow-ups.
- Build a short internal course on "non-manager career pathing" for IC growth.

Development notes / behavior evidence (for performance calibration):
- Collaboration: worked with PM (Jonas) and Eng leads to streamline offer approvals — cross-team momentum.
- Ownership: noticed recurring manual step in offer letters, prototyped new template and got legal sign-off in 2 weeks.
- Impact orientation: prioritized onboarding cohort that removed friction and produced measurable ramp improvements.
- Things to improve: delegate more of the scheduling & logistics to coordinator (I still run too many meeting ops myself).

Self-rating sketch (for draft self-review):
- Competency: Meets expectations -> pushing toward "exceeds" on hiring process metrics.
- Evidence: metrics above + 3 direct manager/peer kudos in #people-ops.

Manager 1:1 agenda (proposed, bring to the meeting):
1) Quick status updates (2–3 min) — offer velocity, cohort status, hiring pipeline risks.
2) Ask: permission to start cross-functional SLA project (high level ask + resourcing: 0.2 FTE from product ops for 6 weeks).
3) Career conversation (10 min) — share stretch goals and ask for a mentorship connection to Head of Talent Ops.
4) Feedback request (5 min) — specific ask: "Where do you see the biggest gaps in my manager/leader readiness?"
5) Blockers & support (5 min) — coordination bandwidth and legal review queue for new templates.

Notes-to-self (immediate TODOs):
- Draft SLA one-pager outline (deadline: 2026-03-20).
- Create candidate comms template + automated checklist (prototype: 2026-03-25).
- Add 2 evidence snippets to self-review doc (links to offers J-58, onboarding cohort survey) — by 2026-03-18.
- Delegate recurring meeting scheduling to Emma (hr-coordinator) and document SOP.

Open questions I want manager help with:
- Can we get 0.2 FTE from Product Ops to help run the SLA interviews? (If not, what's realistic?)
- Is it the right time to propose the internal non-manager course? Budget constraints?
- How does leadership want performance narratives framed across FY26 (metrics-first vs story-first)?

Risk / mitigation plan for hiring funnel (notes):
- Risk: market salary pressure for certain senior infra roles — mitigation: propose reserve flex budget for top-of-band offers and speed hiring cadence. Draft proposal to discuss with finance.

Calibration prep (for upcoming review meeting):
- Evidence bundle to attach: offer time series (CSV), cohort survey export, manager office-hours attendance, peer kudos screenshots.
- Short narratives < 150 words tying each metric to business impact.

Random ideas / brain-dump (notes to return to):
- Micro-mentorship program: match new managers with senior managers for 1-session problem solving.
- Quick "offer thermometers" spreadsheet that visualizes candidate lag by step and owner.
- Short checklist card to include in hiring packet: "3 things to do in week 1 to avoid onboarding friction".

Closing note to self:
- Keep this doc rough; transfer high-confidence bullets into the formal self-review template next week. Use empirical evidence when available.
- Remind manager of timeline for SLA one-pager in 2 weeks.

Unresolved items to follow up after 1:1:
- Confirm mentor intro to Head of Talent Ops (Priya).
- Align on the hiring SLA pilot scope and success metrics.

---
Revision history (short):
- 2026-02-10: initial draft
- 2026-03-12: added cohort metric, updated time-to-offer numbers, queued 1:1 agenda
